steps.name: QC + DESeq2 treated vs control
caveats: DESeq2 requires unique rownames; featureCounts can emit duplicate gene IDs — deduplicate (keep the first row) and report how many duplicates were removed.
Verify the 6 count-matrix sample columns match the 6 metadata rows exactly; fail loudly on any mismatch instead of silently reordering.
n=3 per group gives limited power: expect many genes at nominal p<0.05 and far fewer at FDR<0.05 — report effect sizes and do not over-interpret a small significant set.
Do not manually pre-filter low-count genes; let DESeq2's independent filtering run and report how many genes it filtered.
steps.context: Files: /eval-four-models-v2-without-star-counts-n3-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 x 7: one gene-ID column plus 6 sample columns; raw integer counts from STAR alignments + featureCounts — gene-level, not transcript-level) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-star-counts-n3-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (6 x 2: one row per sample with a condition column; 3 treated, 3 control). Organism Homo sapiens (taxon 9606), tissue liver, unpaired, single batch. Row-ID space is not stated in the profile (featureCounts typically emits Ensembl gene IDs) — detect it from the file and map to HGNC symbols with org.Hs.eg.db, reporting the mapping rate.
steps.question: Which of the 12,000 genes in /eval-four-models-v2-without-star-counts-n3-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv are differentially expressed between the 3 treated and 3 control human liver samples, using the condition labels in /eval-four-models-v2-without-star-counts-n3-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv?
constraints: Use the gene-level featureCounts counts as the DE input directly (integer, as-is); do NOT use tximport or any transcript-level quantification step.
Model: design ~ condition only — two-group, unpaired, single batch. No batch covariate, no pairing term.
Report apeglm-shrunken log2FC in the primary table alongside the unshrunken estimate.
Primary significance: BH FDR < 0.05; secondary: nominal p < 0.05, both split into up- and down-regulated lists.
Export the full 12,000-gene ranked table to CSV, not only significant rows.
No network access: use only the provided files and installed packages.
steps.description: Per-sample QC on the raw featureCounts counts (12,000 genes x 6 samples, integer), then two-group DESeq2 differential expression of treated vs control with apeglm log2FC shrinkage, plus gene-ID to HGNC symbol mapping. Produces: a full 12,000-gene ranked DE table (shrunken and unshrunken log2FC, Wald p, BH FDR, baseMean, symbol), primary (FDR<0.05) and secondary (nominal p<0.05) DE lists split by direction, a per-sample QC table, and a PCA plot of the 3v3 grouping.
acceptance_criteria: Per-sample QC table (library size, fraction of genes detected) with any deviant sample flagged rather than silently dropped.
DE table with one row per gene containing log2FC (apeglm), unshrunken log2FC, p-value, BH FDR, baseMean, and mapped gene symbol.
Reported counts of genes with FDR<0.05 (up/down) and nominal p<0.05 (up/down), plus a top-10-by-|Wald-statistic| example per direction.
PCA of variance-stabilized counts showing (or honestly documenting) the 3-treated vs 3-control grouping.
Symbol mapping rate reported; unmapped genes retained in the full table under their original IDs.

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes (human)
caveats: With n=3 per group the FDR<0.05 DE set may be very small; ORA on fewer than ~10 genes is unreliable — treat the nominal list and the ranked GSEA as the more robust evidence and say so in the result.
Parse the GMT first column on '%' before using set names; the raw descriptor is 'name%WP_ID%species'.
WikiPathways sets vary widely in size; very large or very small sets can dominate ORA — report set sizes in the output table.
steps.context: Inputs: the full ranked DE table and the primary/secondary DE symbol lists produced by T1S1. Reference: a human pathway gene-set collection in GMT format (WikiPathways Homo sapiens), provisioned in the reference store under the wikipathways-human group — resolve it against the store at run time; its first GMT column is a '%'-delimited descriptor (name%WikiPathways-ID%species), so split on '%' to recover the set name. The dataset is human (taxon 9606); the gene-set organism must match. The store also holds mouse and rat WikiPathways files — do not use those.
steps.question: Which human pathways are over-represented among the up- and down-regulated differentially expressed genes from T1S1, and which pathways are enriched by ranked GSEA across the full 12,000-gene list?
constraints: Use only human gene sets; verify the organism on the GMT descriptor before running any test.
ORA must be direction-split (up-regulated vs down-regulated separately); report the input-gene count per test and use a minimum set size.
GSEA ranking: all genes ranked by the signed DESeq2 Wald statistic — never by unsigned p-value.
Significance threshold: BH FDR < 0.1 for enriched sets; report exact FDR values, not rounded.
If the human gene-set collection is absent at run time, report the absence explicitly and stop that part of the step; do not substitute a non-human or differently-species collection.
steps.description: Functional characterization of the treated-vs-control result: ORA on the direction-split DE symbol lists (FDR<0.05 primary; nominal p<0.05 if the primary set is too small) plus ranked GSEA on the full gene list ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic. Gene sets: the provisioned human WikiPathways gene-set collection (GMT format, HGNC symbols).
acceptance_criteria: ORA tables (separate for up- and down-regulated genes) with set size, enriched-member list, p-value, and FDR.
Ranked GSEA table with NES and FDR per pathway.
Reported count of significant sets at FDR<0.1 per direction, or an explicit statement that none reached it.
Recorded confirmation that the gene-set collection is human before any test ran.

plan.title: Liver treated-vs-control DE + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: Human liver bulk RNA-seq, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch, raw integer gene-level counts from STAR+featureCounts (12,000 genes x 6 samples in counts.csv, condition labels in metadata.csv). Because the counts are already gene-level (not transcript-level from a quantifier), DESeq2 consumes them directly — no tximport. Step T1S1 does per-sample QC, then a two-group DESeq2 design with apeglm-shrunken log2FC, and maps row IDs to HGNC symbols, answering 'which genes are differentially expressed'. Step T1S2 characterizes the result with human WikiPathways enrichment (ORA on direction-split DE sets + ranked GSEA on the full list), which is the more robust evidence given n=3 per group will yield a small FDR-significant set.
